title: Year 12 Chemistry Module 8 – Applying Chemical Ideas
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Chemistry Module 8, organised by its three Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How are environmental ions identified & measured?

questions.prompt: What test identifies some metal ions from the colour they produce in a flame?
What type of reaction forms an insoluble solid that can help identify an ion?
What term describes identifying which substances are present without measuring their amount?
What term describes measuring how much of a substance is present?
What analytical method determines an amount by measuring the mass of a precipitate?
What titration method determines an ion concentration by forming a precipitate?
What technique measures light absorbance to determine the concentration of a coloured species?
What technique measures absorption by free atoms to determine concentrations of metal ions?

categories.name: How is organic structure & reactivity determined?

questions.prompt: What test reagent is rapidly decolourised by many compounds containing a carbon–carbon double bond?
What spectroscopy identifies functional groups using characteristic bond vibrations?
What technique separates ions by mass-to-charge ratio and gives a molecular fragmentation pattern?
What spectroscopy gives information about chemical environments of carbon or hydrogen nuclei?
Which NMR technique focuses on carbon-13 nuclei?
Which NMR technique focuses on hydrogen-1 nuclei?
In a mass spectrum, what peak usually corresponds to the intact molecular ion?
questions.answer: The molecular ion peak. Accept: M⁺ peak.

questions.prompt: What region of an IR spectrum contains a complex pattern often useful for confirming compound identity?

categories.name: What are the implications of synthesis & design?

questions.prompt: What term describes the percentage of theoretical product actually obtained?
What term describes how free a chemical product is from unwanted substances?
What concept measures how efficiently reactant atoms are incorporated into the desired product?
What broad approach aims to design chemical processes that reduce hazardous substances and waste?
What industrial process synthesises ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen?
What industrial process is used to manufacture sulfuric acid?
What factor asks whether the required starting materials can be obtained for a synthesis?
Environmental, social and economic effects are collectively examples of what when evaluating a synthesis?

finalRound.prompt: What analytical technique uses proton and carbon-13 signals to reveal different chemical environments within an organic molecule?
finalRound.answer: NMR spectroscopy. Accept: nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
